description:
For more than a decade, governments got used to cheap borrowing. That era may now be ending.

Government bond markets are flashing warnings around the world.

Across major economies, yields - the interest rates governments pay to borrow - are climbing to levels not seen in years and, in some cases, decades.

Investors are pricing in more risk before they'll lend to governments already carrying heavy debt loads.

Inflation remains stubborn, geopolitical tensions are adding pressure, and central banks may have to keep interest rates higher for longer.

Those higher borrowing costs are pushing up what banks charge companies and homeowners.

The Bab al-Mandab Strait is one of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints, linking Asia and Europe through the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

Presenter Dalya Al Masri explains how Houthi forces, also known as Ansar Allah, have seized key coastal positions including the port of Mocka and Mayun Island, giving them significant leverage over the narrow passage.

Around 12% of international commerce passes through the Bab al-Mandab. Any disruption could force ships to take a much longer route around Africa, increasing fuel costs and transit times.

With tensions also rising around the Strait of Hormuz, control of the Bab al-Mandab has become increasingly important to global shipping, trade and regional geopolitics.

Dangote has described the sale as a way to spread prosperity by bringing millions of new shareholders into the business rather than simply raising money for the company. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Muslim-majority Bangsamoro region in the southern Philippines is holding its first parliamentary election, the final step in its transition to self-governance. The separatist Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) signed a peace deal with the government in 2014, ending decades of conflict, and has run the region under an interim government since 2019. Now it is contesting 80 seats in the new parliament.

Peace has remained fragile: in 2016, ISIL-linked fighters briefly seized one town, and in August, Bangsamoro's chief minister survived an ambush, prompting checkpoints across the region. Poverty has halved under MILF's interim rule, but Bangsamoro remains one of the Philippines' poorest regions. Political dynasties that governed before 2019 are also contesting seats, arguing they can better serve their communities. Voters say lasting peace remains the only path to progress.

Al Jazeera's Barnaby Lo reports from Butig, Lanao del Sur, in the southern Philippines.

title: Bangsamoro holds first election as fears of renewed conflict linger

Since then, thousands have been killed or disappeared, with searchers like the volunteer group Sabuesos Guerreras digging through the countryside using little more than metal ground drills, often without government support. Criminals here have a saying: "If there's no body, there's no crime."

US President Donald Trump has met Ireland's leaders during a visit in which he said he would "love" to see a united Ireland and discussed the war with Iran. The visit drew protests in Dublin and in the west, where Trump travelled to his golf resort for the Irish Open.

Polls suggest Trump is deeply unpopular in Ireland, and protesters marched through central Dublin to parliament, objecting to his visit and, in some cases, to Irish leaders meeting him given Ireland's stance on Palestine. By afternoon, Trump was in Doonbeg, where his resort brings welcome business, and he is popular. Despite divided opinion, few in Ireland dispute the importance of the US relationship.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The CEO of one of the world's largest AI companies says research into the technology should slow down. Anthropic's Dario Amodei says AI systems are becoming too sophisticated for humans to control, a call echoed by OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk. 

Toby Walsh, chief scientist of the AI Institute at the University of New South Wales, says the "kill us all" scenario is fantastical, but dangerous capabilities are real, citing an Anthropic report on bad actors using its bot for bioweapon research. He points to massive spending, over a billion dollars a day, and newly discovered "swarms" of coordinating AI agents as drivers of the risk.

Walsh says race dynamics between companies have blocked regulation, though firms increasingly welcome oversight themselves. Still, the UK has rejected a proposed AI "kill switch," and similar resistance exists in the US, driven partly by fears of losing ground to China.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iranian media report that Iran will brief Gulf countries on its negotiations with Oman at a meeting scheduled for Monday. Tehran and Muscat have held talks in recent weeks to draw up a framework for managing the Strait of Hormuz, though Iranian media say any agreement will not mean the waterway reopens immediately. Iran, Iraq and other Gulf states are expected to attend, though Bahrain has said it will not.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, told Al Jazeera the meeting will brief regional delegations on the results of the Iran-Oman consultations on safe passage through the strait.

Mohammad Eslami, a research fellow in Middle East and North Africa studies at Tehran University, says the talks cover legal and logistical aspects that need explaining to other stakeholders, even though the underlying agreement is bilateral. He notes the situation remains fragile, pointing to Donald Trump's threats of sanctions or strikes against Oman over any deal with Iran. Eslami say
title: Iran to brief Gulf states on Oman talks over Strait of Hormuz: Analysis

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Yemen's internationally recognised government says its forces carried out more than 20 air strikes on Houthi positions on Saturday, part of a counteroffensive along the western coast after the group, formally known as Ansar Allah, captured several towns and islands in recent days. 

The Houthis seized the port city of Mokha on Thursday, gaining a foothold on the Red Sea coast after government forces withdrew, and fighters reached the strategic Mayun Island in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait on Friday.

Al Jazeera's Youssef Mawry, reporting from Sana'a, says Saudi-backed government forces are relying on air strikes rather than ground battles because troops in the area have largely withdrawn, letting the Houthis advance further. The group has said only Saudi vessels will be blocked from the strait, with other countries free to pass.
